name: MathlibAnnex.PluckerBody.body
title: The symmetric convex body of contraction minors

content.display_title: The symmetric convex body of contraction minors
content.one_sentence_role: Takes the real convex hull of both signs of every contraction generator.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n,N\in\mathbb N_0$ and give $E=\mathbb R^n$ and $F=\mathbb R^N$ their coordinate sup norms. Let $\lambda_n$ be the fixed coordinate Lebesgue measure on $E$. Let $p:E\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous real seminorm with specified constants $a_p,b_p>0$ such that
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty\qquad(x\in E).$$

The lower bound makes $p$ a norm. Its closed unit ball and real reference volume are
$$K_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\},\qquad v_p=\lambda_n(K_p)\in(0,\infty).$$
Here and below a finite Lebesgue measure is read as a real number when used as a scalar.

Let $\mathcal I_{n,N}$ be the finite set of increasing $n$-tuples of distinct rows from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. The minor-coordinate space $\mathbb R^{\mathcal I_{n,N}}$ carries its sup norm. For a linear map $B:E\to F$, put $B_{ij}=(Be_j)_i$ in the standard coordinate basis. Write $\Pi_n(B)$ for its maximal-minor vector and $\mathcal V_p(B)$ for that vector scaled by $v_p$. Their coordinates and scaling are
$$\Pi_n(B)_I=\det(B_{i_a,j})_{a,j=1}^n,\qquad\mathcal V_p(B)=v_p\Pi_n(B)\quad(I=(i_1<\cdots<i_n)).$$

A $p$-contraction is a linear map $B:E\to F$ satisfying $\|Bz\|_\infty\le p(z)$ for every $z\in E$. Write $\mathcal C_p^N$ for these maps. Write $\mathcal G_p^N$ for the signed generator set and $\mathcal P_p^N$ for its real convex hull, so
$$\mathcal G_p^N=\{\mathcal V_p(B),-\mathcal V_p(B):B\in\mathcal C_p^N\},\qquad\mathcal P_p^N=\operatorname{conv}_{\mathbb R}(\mathcal G_p^N).$$
content.definition_explanation:
For each integer $\ell\ge1$, choose weights $t_1,\ldots,t_\ell\ge0$ with sum $1$, signs $\varepsilon_k\in\{-1,1\}$, and maps $B_k\in\mathcal C_p^N$. The body consists of all resulting finite convex combinations:
$$\mathcal P_p^N=\left\{\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}t_k\varepsilon_k\mathcal V_p(B_k):
\begin{array}{l}\ell\ge1,\ t_k\ge0,\ \sum_{k=1}^{\ell}t_k=1,\\
\varepsilon_k\in\{-1,1\},\ B_k\in\mathcal C_p^N\end{array}\right\}.$$
The [signed-generator definition](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L18-L24) is a separate declaration. The exact RHS of the present definition takes its real convex hull.
content.assumptions: The source and target are finite real coordinate spaces with sup norms. The seminorm $p$ is continuous and has the stated positive lower and upper comparison constants. The measure is the original coordinate Lebesgue measure. The dimensions $n,N$ may be zero. When $n=0$, the unique empty minor has determinant $1$; when $N<n$, the minor-index set is empty and its function space has one element. Neither case is excluded.
content.conclusion: This declaration defines $\mathcal P_p^N$. Compactness and average membership are separate theorems.
content.lean_realization_notes: The zero map is a contraction, so [generator nonemptiness](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L30-L32) supplies $\mathcal V_p(0)\in\mathcal G_p^N$; this vector need not be zero when $n=0$. The two alternatives give [generator sign symmetry](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L34-L39). Consequently [body sign symmetry](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L41-L50) says $z\in\mathcal P_p^N\Rightarrow-z\in\mathcal P_p^N$: negate each generator in a convex combination while keeping its nonnegative weights.
